source_description: Waverly, IA June 17, 2008 -- FEMA intergovernmental Affairs representative, Jim Woodard, talks residents of Waverly, IA at a town hall meeting. FEMA is working with State and local officials to help with the rebuilding of the town after it was flooded when the Cedar River came over its' banks. Photo by Patsy Lynch/FEMA
caption: Jim Woodard, an intergovernmental affairs representative for the Federal Emergency Management Agency, speaks at a town hall meeting for residents of Waverly, Iowa, on June 17, 2008, after the Cedar River flooded the town. Photograph: Patsy Lynch, FEMA.
why_it_fits: People doing public work, officials among them: a named federal official speaks at a town hall, with a panel seated behind him. A different region, agency and year from the recommended photograph.
notes: The agency caption names Woodard but does not say where he stands; the standing speaker with the microphone is the only person speaking. The seated panel is not named, so the caption must not name them. The audience is out of frame.
